name: Capillary-Lymphatic Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Capillary-Lymphatic Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of congenital or early childhood onset of mixed capillary and lymphatic vascular lesions presenting as soft, compressible, bluish or pinkish skin lesions
MRI or ultrasound demonstrating combined capillary and lymphatic vascular malformations with characteristic cystic and microvascular components
Biopsy showing abnormal proliferation of capillary and lymphatic endothelial-lined channels without evidence of malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus confirmatory imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic but may support diagnosis in syndromic cases

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mixed capillary and lymphatic vascular skin lesions
searchTerms: skin lesions with mixed blood and lymph vessels
vascular skin spots combining capillaries and lymphatics

pathognomonic.symptomName: Soft, compressible, bluish or pinkish cutaneous plaques

common.symptomName: Localized swelling due to lymphatic fluid accumulation
Pain or discomfort at lesion site
Recurrent episodes of cellulitis or infection in affected area

occasional.symptomName: Functional impairment due to lesion size or location
Bleeding or oozing from superficial lesions
Localized warmth or erythema over lesion

rare.symptomName: Compression of adjacent neurovascular structures causing neuropathy

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated inflammatory markers during infection
imaging: MRI showing combined capillary and lymphatic malformations with cystic and microvascular components
Doppler ultrasound demonstrating low-flow vascular malformation
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; somatic mutations in PIK3CA pathway reported in some cases
other: Histopathology revealing abnormal capillary and lymphatic channels without malignancy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly venous channels without significant lymphatic involvement
Typically darker blue lesions with slower flow on Doppler imaging
Purely lymphatic cystic lesions without capillary component
Often presents as macrocystic or microcystic masses without superficial telangiectasias

references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams DM, et al. Vascular Anomalies Classification: Recommendations From the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015
